title: Yochanan Chakuka’ah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Pesachim 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.13a.11): he came before Rabbi to ask about a bag full of chametz that someone had deposited with him and that mice had pierced, etc. In the Yerushalmi there, chapter 1, halakhah 4, the incident is told as follows: a man deposited a bag of chametz with R. Ch. Rabbah; R. Y. bar Bun said, ‘It was Yochanan Chakukya.’ And in Bava Metzia, chapter 3, halakhah 4: R. Yochanan Chakukah deposited chametz with R. Ch. Rubba; he asked Rabbi, etc.[^1]

Pesachim 53b relates that he once went out to the villages. They asked him whether the wheat had done well, and he answered that the barley had done well. The reply was, ‘Go and bring the good news to the horses and donkeys.’ There R. Ch. explains that he was a scribe, while R. Y. explains that he was from the town of Chakukah.[^2]

notes.text: The heading and the quoted accounts spell the name differently: חקוקאה, חקוקיא, and חקוקה. These forms, and the epithets רבה and רובא, are retained distinctly. The initials R. Ch. (ר״ח) and R. Y. (ר״י) are not expanded here. Hyman’s two Yerushalmi accounts differ over who deposited the chametz and who received it; the translation preserves both rather than reconciling them.

The commentator initials in the final paragraph need not identify the same people as those in the preceding accounts. The speaker of the reply about horses and donkeys is not named in Hyman’s summary. Pesachim 13a was checked in the William Davidson edition; the other locators are reproduced as Hyman’s citations, without an independent passage check.
